Comment: CloudLab c240g5 (scripts/cloudlab/profile.py: node0 the control node, node1 to node4 the hosts of n1 to n4): the Quake example of the update strategies -- a round of Quake's maintenance planned after each batch and run as a major epoch (internal/update/quake.go: its cost model, on the hits of the entries' last 10,000 client queries, decides which lists to delete and split; the splits' neighbourhoods are refined; empty lists are removed) -- on Wikipedia c1024, 4 data nodes, the load constant. The update experiment's four minor batches of the 2026-02 diff (b4x5: 775K inserts and about 744K deletes each, 400 s apart: experiment.wiki-c1024-cloudlab-gpu-updates.json), each followed by its round of Quake's maintenance, decided once on this cluster and saved (experiment.wiki-c1024-kmeans-cloudlab-gpu-quake-plans.json: a plan runs only on the state it was decided on, and the batches' routing is this control node's; "Quake": {"Plan": FILE}, rtier-updater -quake-plan, internal/update/quakeplan.go): each epoch reads its lists, checks that they hold what they held when the round was decided, and runs the round's edits, deciding nothing; no full rebuild and no spare. On Quake's index of Wikipedia c1024: a flat k-means of round(sqrt(N)) = 3,939 lists, one replica a vector (fusion_build --from-index the base index --clustering kmeans; the base's IDs, raw-vector locations, codebook and page file; results/kmeans-index-2026-11-26), its 64 GP partitions with each head weighing its list's postings, the nodes started on its 4-node warmup snapshot (experiment.wiki-c1024-kmeans-cloudlab-gpu-warmup-4.json); inserts go to their nearest head. Quake's parameters are its Wikipedia configuration's (Quake's repository, test/experiments/osdi2025/wiki_workload/configs/wiki.yaml, the configurations with maintenance: window_size 10000, refinement_radius 50, split_threshold_ns 250, delete_threshold_ns 500000, enable_delete_rejection false), one refinement iteration, as its paper runs it (§7.2), the rest its defaults; its nc 1000 is not taken (the paper sizes its indexes at sqrt(|X0|)), nor its metric (ip; ours is L2). QuerySample 2500: the 4 entries keep the window's 10,000 queries. Rate 520 = 0.6 x C4 of this index, floored to tens (C4 867 q/s at nprobe 96 on the reservation of 2026-11-20: experiment.wiki-c1024-kmeans-cloudlab-gpu-calibrate-4.json, results/cloudlab-gpu/2026-11-26-quake/calibrate-4). NProbe, with --max-nprobe the same (the GPU's candidate buffers), is the smallest that reaches the base index's recall at nprobe 64, N 200 (0.8891), from the lab server's recall table (results/kmeans-index-2026-11-26/summary.txt): 96 (recall 0.9108). Answers are scored per data version (scripts/score_answers.py) against <GroundTruth>.versions/ (2026-11-22: the same batches, IDs and locations). UpdateLease 60m and StageTimeout 60m. GraphHeadroom 10: the rounds split thousands of lists (2,743 of 3,939 in the first: Quake's cost model, on our scan profile, wants lists several times shorter than sqrt(N)'s; the default room of 0.2 stopped the lab server's first trial), and a deleted head keeps its place in the graph.
